help.intro: Fifteen sentences in the Perfekt, heard and typed. Two things are being trained: hearing the helper — habe / hast / hat / bin / bist / ist / sind — at the start, and writing the participle correctly at the end, ge- and all. The helper gives away the verb's type before you have heard the verb: bin / ist / sind mean a movement or change verb is coming (gefahren, gekommen, aufgestanden). Write the sentence whole, and check the two ends against each other: a sein-helper with a haben-participle means you misheard one of them.
help.tips[0].title: Hear the helper, predict the participle
help.tips[0].text: 'Wir sind …' → a movement verb is coming: gefahren, gegangen, gekommen. 'Ich habe …' → anything else: gesehen, gemacht, gegessen.
help.tips[0].check.q: You hear „Wir sind gestern nach Köln …“. Which word most likely ends the sentence?
help.tips[0].check.why: sind as the helper signals a movement verb, so a participle like gefahren is coming.
help.tips[1].title: ge- is written, even when it is quiet
help.tips[1].text: gegessen, gearbeitet, gefunden — the ge- is unstressed and easy to miss by ear. If the verb is a plain one (no -ieren, no be-/ver-), write ge-.
help.tips[1].check.why: finden is a plain verb, so its participle has ge-: gefunden. Write the quiet ge- even if you barely hear it.
help.tips[2].title: Questions start with the helper
help.tips[2].text: Hast du …? Bist du …? Seid ihr …? The helper is the first word, the participle still the last.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Did you go to the cinema yesterday?
help.tips[2].check.why: The helper (hast) comes first, and the participle (gelesen) stays at the very end.
help.remember[0]: First word and last word belong together: check that they agree.
help.remember[1]: Plain verb → write ge-, whether or not you heard it.
help.exam: A2 Schreiben: the marker checks helpers and participles; dictation trains you to write what a correct sentence sounds like.
help.hook: Write down little stories about the past — once you hear habe or bin, you already know how the sentence will end.
